events.blurb: Santa Eulària's patron-saint festival with around 150 events including children's games, workshops, a solemn mass and procession at Puig de Missa, traditional dancing, street music, tastings and more than 70 concerts across local bars and restaurants.

events.name: Santa Eulària Ibiza Marathon
events.when: annually in April; 2026 edition Saturday 18 April
events.blurb: Road running event with full marathon (42K), 22K and a family-friendly 12K along the Santa Eulària seafront, drawing thousands of runners from many countries. The marathon route starts at the Port of Ibiza.

events.name: Barruguet Family Theatre Festival
events.when: annually in May; 2026 edition 22-24 May
events.blurb: Family-oriented theatre festival in Santa Eulària des Riu with around 20 public performances plus additional shows aimed at schools and care homes, part of the town's May programme.

events.name: Las Dalias Hippy Market (Sant Carles de Peralta)
events.when: every Saturday year-round, plus summer night markets; Christmas market in December
events.blurb: One of Ibiza's largest and best-known markets, running since 1985, with around 300 stalls of crafts, fashion, jewellery, gastronomy and gifts in nearby Sant Carles de Peralta. Saturdays year-round with additional summer night markets.

events.name: Ibiza Medieval Fair (Eivissa Medieval, Dalt Vila)
events.when: annually in May; 2026 edition 7-10 May
events.blurb: Annual medieval fair in the fortified old town (Dalt Vila) of nearby Ibiza Town, turning the streets into a medieval scene with markets, crafts, food, musicians, jugglers and shows.

events.name: Festa Major de Palamós (Sant Joan)
events.when: annually in late June around the feast of Sant Joan; 2026 edition approximately 20-23 June
events.blurb: Palamós's main town festival tied to the Sant Joan midsummer celebrations, with open-air concerts (Barraques on Platja Gran), habaneres, the Flama del Canigó, a bonfire night and closing fireworks.

events.name: Fira de la Gamba de Palamós (Prawn Fair)
events.when: annually in early June at the Port de Palamós fish market; 2025 edition was 7 June
events.blurb: Gastronomy fair celebrating the famous Palamós red prawn, held beside the fish market with tastings, cooking demonstrations and activities promoting the town's fishing heritage and sustainable practices.

events.name: Palamós Terra de Mar - Maritime Festival of the Costa Brava
events.when: annually in May; 2026 edition 23-24 May
events.blurb: A maritime festival celebrating Costa Brava sea culture with boat tours, kayaking, sailing and SUP activities, plus marine-science and underwater-robotics demonstrations from the University of Girona.

events.name: Rumb(A) Palamós - Catalan Rumba Festival
events.when: annually on Fridays during July
events.blurb: Summer music festival featuring free Catalan rumba concerts on Friday evenings throughout July in Palamós.

events.name: Amb So de Cobla Festival
events.when: annually in early August; 2025 edition 5-9 August
events.blurb: Festival of traditional Catalan cobla music held in Palamós each August.

events.name: Virgin of Carmel sea procession (Festa del Carme)
events.when: annually on 16 July
events.blurb: Traditional maritime celebration honouring the Virgin of Carmel, patron saint of fishermen and sailors, with decorated fishing boats taking part in a procession by sea, observed in Palamós and other Costa Brava coastal towns.

events.name: Cantada d'Havaneres de Calella de Palafrugell
events.when: annually on the first Saturday of July at Port Bo beach, Calella de Palafrugell (about 8 km from La Fosca); 58th edition was 5 July 2025
events.blurb: The reference gathering of the havaneres (Catalan sea-shanty) world, a seaside concert at Port Bo beach in nearby Calella de Palafrugell featuring traditional habanera singing and cremat (flamed rum).

events.name: Noite de San Xoán (San Juan Bonfires)
events.when: Annually on the night of 23-24 June; 2026 edition night of 23 June into 24 June
events.blurb: A Coruña's biggest festival, declared of International Tourist Interest, with bonfires lit directly on Riazor, Orzán and Matadero beaches. Over 150,000 people gather for sardine grills, music and the midnight 'Noite da Quema' bonfire ritual followed by fireworks.

events.name: Fiestas de María Pita
events.when: Annually throughout August; 2026 edition runs across August (opening 1 August)
events.blurb: A Coruña's main month-long summer festival held in and around Plaza de María Pita, featuring free concerts, craft fairs, exhibitions and family activities throughout August.

events.name: Festival Noroeste Estrella Galicia
events.when: Annually in early August during the María Pita festivities; 2026 edition 5-10 August
events.blurb: Long-running free live-music festival across several plazas and beaches of A Coruña, celebrating its 40th edition in 2026 with multiple stages of free concerts.

events.name: International Folk Festival 'Cidade da Coruña'
events.when: Annually in August during the María Pita festivities (held since 1987); five days of performances
events.blurb: International folklore festival running since 1987, coinciding with the María Pita fiestas, with participating groups from around the world performing traditional dance and music over five days.

events.name: Medio Maratón Coruña21 (Half Marathon)
events.when: Annually around late February / early March; 2026 (18th edition) on 1 March, 09:30 start
events.blurb: Certified 21.097 km half marathon (plus a 5K race) on a fast, flat seafront circuit, starting at the Obelisco on Cantón Grande and finishing at Plaza de María Pita.

events.name: Entroido (Carnival) of A Coruña
events.when: Annually in February (Carnival week); 2026 edition 13-18 February
events.blurb: A Coruña's carnival week with the enthronement of the Momo God, a grand parade to María Pita, the Choqueiros competition, and the Burial of the Sardine ending at San Amaro beach, plus traditional gastronomy like filloas and orejas.

events.name: Tamborrada (Drum Festival) — San Sebastián Day
events.when: Annually on 20 January (begins at midnight on 19 January); 2026 edition centred on 20 January 2026
events.blurb: A 24-hour drum festival marking the feast day of Saint Sebastian, the city's patron saint. Over 100 bands and 15,000 locals parade through the streets drumming, including a famous children's parade.

events.name: Jazzaldia (San Sebastián Jazz Festival)
events.when: Annually in late July; 2026 edition (61st) around 22-26 July 2026
events.blurb: One of the oldest jazz festivals in Europe, internationally renowned, with concerts across the city including free open-air stages, some near Zurriola beach and the Kursaal.

events.name: Semana Grande / Aste Nagusia (Grand Week)
events.when: Annually the week including 15 August; 2026 edition 8-15 August 2026
events.blurb: San Sebastián's main summer festival with Basque folklore, concerts and street entertainment, including events at the port and around Zurriola beach.

events.name: International Fireworks Competition (Donostia)
events.when: Annually during Semana Grande, nightly at 22:45 over La Concha bay; 2026 edition (60th) 8-15 August 2026
events.blurb: A nightly pyrotechnics contest during Semana Grande where teams compete over La Concha bay for the Concha de Oro prize. Free to watch from the promenades, hillsides and boats.

events.name: San Sebastián Musical Fortnight (Quincena Musical)
events.when: Annually in August; 2026 edition approximately 2-30 August 2026
events.blurb: A classical music season held every summer since 1939, spanning a broad range of styles and composers across venues in the city.

events.name: San Sebastián International Film Festival (Zinemaldia)
events.when: Annually in mid-to-late September; 2026 edition (74th) 18-26 September 2026
events.blurb: A FIAPF A-category film festival on a par with Cannes, Venice and Berlin, centred on the Kursaal next to Zurriola beach, featuring Official Selection screenings and the Donostia Awards.

events.name: Nit de Sant Joan (Midsummer Night)
events.when: annually on the night of 23-24 June; 2026 edition night of 23 June into 24 June
events.blurb: Catalonia's summer solstice celebration with bonfires, firecrackers, fireworks, coca cake and cava. The nearby Mar Bella, Bogatell and Nova Icaria beaches fill with thousands of people partying through the night, making this one of the biggest events right on this stretch of coast.

events.name: Festa Major del Poblenou
events.when: annually in mid-September; 2026 edition runs 5-14 September
events.blurb: The main neighbourhood festival of Poblenou, the district immediately behind the beach, with hundreds of activities, concerts, popular culture, correfocs and street parties across many venues over about ten days.

events.name: Festes de Maig del Poblenou
events.when: annually in May; 48th edition 15-17 May 2026
events.blurb: A long-running spring festival in the Poblenou neighbourhood featuring concerts, children's activities, popular Catalan culture, a wine festival and a fair of local associations and artisans.

events.name: Primavera Sound Barcelona
events.when: annually in early June at Parc del Forum (about 2 km north of the beach); 2026 edition 4-6 June
events.blurb: One of Europe's largest indie, rock and electronic music festivals, held at the Parc del Forum just up the coast from the beach. The 2026 edition features The Cure, Gorillaz, Massive Attack, Doja Cat and Skrillex among many others.

events.name: La Merce Festival
events.when: annually around 24 September (city patron saint day); 2026 edition 23-27 September
events.blurb: Barcelona's largest annual festival honouring the city's patron saint, the Mare de Deu de la Merce, with castellers (human towers), correfocs, giants, concerts and fireworks across the city. The 2026 guest city is Manchester.

events.name: Carnaval de Cádiz
events.when: annually in February (movable, before Lent); 2026 edition 12-22 February, with fireworks over La Caleta on the main parade Sundays
events.blurb: One of Spain's most famous carnivals, declared an International Tourist Attraction. Ten days of choirs (coros), comparsas and satirical chirigotas, street singing, parades and fireworks, some of them launched over Playa de la Caleta.

events.name: Procession of the Virgen del Carmen
events.when: annually on 16 July
events.blurb: Maritime-religious festival honouring the patron of sailors. The image of the Virgin is carried out from Playa de la Caleta and taken around the bay of Cádiz by boat, escorted by a flotilla of fishing vessels, with bands and fireworks.

events.name: Entierro de la Caballa (Burial of the Mackerel)
events.when: annually in late August (around 22-25 August), marking the end of summer
events.blurb: A mock funeral procession winds through the La Viña neighbourhood carrying a giant wooden mackerel that is finally burned on Playa de la Caleta. Includes a free public tasting of noodles with mackerel and carnival performances on the beach.

events.name: Trofeo Carranza (Ramón de Carranza Trophy)
events.when: annually in early-to-mid August at the Nuevo Mirandilla stadium
events.blurb: Long-running international pre-season football tournament hosted by Cádiz CF, drawing top invited clubs. The matches turn the city into a festival with concerts, family activities and a beach-party atmosphere.

events.name: Semana Santa de Cádiz (Holy Week)
events.when: annually during Holy Week (March/April, movable); 2026 falls 29 March-5 April
events.blurb: Solemn Holy Week processions of brotherhoods carrying ornate floats through the historic centre of Cádiz, close to Playa de la Caleta, with music and incense over several days.

events.name: Formentera Jazz Festival
events.when: annually in early June; 2026 edition (12th) runs 4-7 June 2026, with free open-air concerts in Sant Francesc, Blue Bar, Sa Panxa and Ses Roques
events.blurb: Free four-day jazz festival held at emblematic spots across Formentera, including Sant Francesc square and seaside venues. Winner of the 2025 Balearic Islands Tourism Award for Best Tourist Experience.

events.name: Festes de Sant Joan (La Mola)
events.when: annually around 23-24 June, with celebrations through late June in El Pilar de la Mola; bonfire night on 23-24 June
events.blurb: Traditional midsummer festival in El Pilar de la Mola featuring the giant Sant Joan bonfire, gaita payesa folk music, concerts, traditional dances and workshops.

events.name: Festes de Sant Ferran de ses Roques
events.when: annually around 30 May in Sant Ferran de ses Roques
events.blurb: Patron-saint festivities of Sant Ferran, the village nearest Platja de Migjorn, with a procession, concerts, traditional dancing, a market in the church square and children's activities.

events.name: La Mola Artisan (Hippy) Market
events.when: every Wednesday and Sunday from May to October, 16:00-22:00, in El Pilar de la Mola
events.blurb: Long-running craft and art market (established 1984) in El Pilar de la Mola, with handmade fashion, jewellery and crafts plus live music, storytelling and local food.

events.name: Festes de la Mare de Deu del Pilar (El Pilar de la Mola)
events.when: annually around 12 October in El Pilar de la Mola, traditionally coinciding with the autumn pig-slaughter season
events.blurb: Autumn patron festival of Our Lady of Pilar in El Pilar de la Mola, with fairs, concerts and traditional gastronomy events.

events.name: Mercat Medieval de Capdepera (Medieval Market)
events.when: annually in mid-May; 2026 edition 15-17 May 2026
events.blurb: Long-running medieval-themed festival held within and around Capdepera's hilltop castle, with costumed performers, artisan craft stalls, falconry, fire shows and traditional food. First held in 2000 to commemorate the castle's founding.

events.name: Festes de Sant Roc (Cala Rajada)
events.when: annually in mid-August, roughly 8-16 August
events.blurb: Cala Rajada's main summer patron-saint festival with open-air dances, concerts, correfocs (fire runs), children's activities, contests, gastronomic events and sports over about a week.

events.name: Festival Serenates d'Estiu de Cala Rajada
events.when: annually in summer (July-August), concert series
events.blurb: Long-established summer concert series organised by Joventuts Musicals de Capdepera (founded 1988), held in the gardens of the Fundació Bartomeu March, featuring classical, chamber, baroque, jazz and fusion music with national and international artists.

events.name: Mostra de la Llampuga (Gold Mackerel / Mahi-Mahi Festival)
events.when: annually on the second weekend of October
events.blurb: Traditional gastronomy fair in Cala Rajada celebrating the local llampuga (mahi-mahi) fish, with cooking shows and tastings, habanera music contests, craft demonstrations and a trade fair.

events.name: Festes del Turista (Capdepera & Cala Rajada)
events.when: annually in late September
events.blurb: Festival held to thank holidaymakers visiting Capdepera and Cala Rajada, with markets, music, dance, gastronomy and cultural activities bringing locals and tourists together.

events.name: Illes Balears Ballooning Festival (Capdepera)
events.when: annually in late October (around 22-26 October)
events.blurb: International hot-air balloon festival based in Capdepera, with pilots and teams from across Europe, morning and evening flights, exhibitions and family activities over several days.

events.name: Fiestas del Carmen Playa Blanca
events.when: annually mid-July, main day around 16 July; includes a grand maritime procession of decorated boats along the southern coast
events.blurb: Playa Blanca's main patron festival honouring the Virgen del Carmen, patroness of fishermen. Features a solemn mass, street procession, a maritime procession of decorated boats along Lanzarote's southern coast, concerts and open-air dances.

events.name: Playa Blanca Carnival (Carnaval de Playa Blanca)
events.when: annually in late winter/early spring; 2026 edition 12-15 March, theme 'The Gods of Olympus', Grand Parade on Saturday 14 March
events.blurb: Southern Lanzarote's lively carnival in Playa Blanca with a Grand Parade, live music concerts and free events on Av. Papagayo. The 2026 theme is 'The Gods of Olympus' and the main parade falls on Saturday 14 March.

events.name: Fiestas de San Marcial del Rubicon (Femes)
events.when: annually late June to early July, main day 7 July, in the village of Femes above Playa Blanca
events.blurb: Religious and cultural festival in the hilltop village of Femes honouring San Marcial del Rubicon, patron saint of Lanzarote. Includes mass, procession, folklore and traditional music, held roughly 10 km from Playa Blanca beach.

events.name: Sinsal SON Estrella Galicia
events.when: annually in late July on San Simón island in the Ría de Vigo; 2026 edition expanded to two weekends, 24-26 July and 31 July-2 August
events.blurb: Boutique music festival held on the island of San Simón in the Vigo estuary, famous for keeping its line-up secret until the audience disembarks on the island.

events.name: O Marisquiño
events.when: annually in early-to-mid August at Samil beach, Vigo (facing the Cíes Islands); 2026 edition 6-9 August
events.blurb: Southern Europe's largest free urban-culture and action-sports festival, with skate, BMX, breaking and 3x3 basketball competitions plus music and gastronomy, centred on Samil beach with the Cíes Islands as a backdrop.

events.name: Festa da Reconquista de Vigo
events.when: annually in late March in Vigo's old town; main days 27-29 March, with the central date on 28 March (2026)
events.blurb: Festival of National Tourist Interest re-enacting the 1809 popular uprising that expelled Napoleon's troops from the city, with period costumes, street markets, traditional music and dance.

events.name: Galicia Fest
events.when: annually in late June at the Peirao de Trasatlánticos, Vigo; 2026 edition 26-27 June
events.blurb: Two-day pop and Latin music festival on Vigo's transatlantic quay, featuring a multi-artist Spanish and Latin American line-up.

events.name: Festival Aéreo Internacional de Vigo (Vigo International Airshow)
events.when: annually in summer (typically July-August) over Samil beach, Vigo, facing the Cíes Islands
events.blurb: Large free international airshow flown over Samil beach and the Vigo estuary, drawing well over 100,000 spectators with aerobatic and military display teams.

events.name: San Xoán (Saint John's Eve / Summer Solstice)
events.when: annually on the night of 23 June, with bonfires on Vigo's beaches and across Galicia
events.blurb: Traditional midsummer celebration welcoming the solstice with beach bonfires (cacharelas), music and seasonal food along the Vigo coastline.
